Landing.headline: Give your AI coding agent the guardrails you wish it came with.
Landing.lede: Answer a short questionnaire about what you're building. Get a ready-to-drop-in skill pack for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or any agent that reads AGENTS.md — covering Saudi compliance, security hygiene, and architecture discipline.
Landing.microcopy: Takes about 3 minutes. No account. Nothing leaves your browser.
Landing.whatIsTitle: What’s a skill, and why do I want one?
Landing.whatIsBody: When an AI coding agent opens your repo, it looks for instructions. A skill is a short, focused document — sometimes with helper scripts — that tells the agent the rules for one specific domain: how to handle invoices in Saudi Arabia, how to keep secrets out of commits, where to draw the line between admin and user code. Good skills turn an agent from “smart intern” into “teammate who read the handbook.”
Landing.featuresAriaLabel: What Wathba Skills does for you
Landing.feature1Body: Answers to stack, payments, and PII questions rewrite the skill so Node/Django/Laravel projects get guidance that actually matches their code.
Landing.feature2Body: Saudi skills (ZATCA Phase 2, PDPL, Nafath) ship with disclaimers, source links, and a verification date — never stale and never silent.
Landing.feature3Body: Pick Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or plain AGENTS.md. Same canonical content, rendered for the target you actually use.
Landing.libraryLede: Every skill is versioned, dated, and reviewed. Draft items are clearly marked — use them as starting points, not gospel.

market.title: Which market does the product primarily serve?
market.desc: We use this to decide whether to recommend Saudi-specific compliance skills.
market.why: Saudi compliance skills (ZATCA, PDPL, Nafath) only make sense when you are operating under KSA law. Pick Global if you want to skip those and keep only the universally useful security and architecture guidance.

ksa.label: Saudi Arabia
ksa.desc: Operating under KSA law; customers or invoicing inside the Kingdom.

gcc.label: Broader GCC
gcc.desc: Gulf markets — some Saudi rules still apply if you invoice in KSA.

global.label: Global / Other
global.desc: Skip Saudi-specific rules; keep security and architecture skills.

invoicing.title: Do you issue invoices to customers in Saudi Arabia?
invoicing.desc: Selling anything — physical, digital, or a subscription — counts.
invoicing.why: If you invoice in KSA, ZATCA Phase 2 requires specific XML formatting, cryptographic stamps, and integration with a government portal. The skill walks your agent through what that means for your stack.

pii.title: Do you store personal data about users?
pii.desc: Names, emails, phone numbers, national IDs, location — any of it.
pii.why: If yes, PDPL (Saudi) and similar privacy rules shape how you handle storage, retention, consent, and access control. We will add the PDPL basics skill.

payments.title: Do you accept payments in the product?
payments.desc: Credit cards, mada, STC Pay, Apple Pay, bank transfers — any of them.
payments.why: Payment flows have specific security and operational rules. mada and STC Pay in particular have local quirks that most generic payment tutorials miss.

identity.title: Do you verify user identity (KYC)?
identity.desc: Onboarding flows, account verification, age-gating, trust signals.
identity.why: Nafath and Yakeen are the Saudi government-run identity services. They are gated — you cannot just call an API. The skill tells your agent the hard parts upfront so it does not invent fake endpoints.

stack.title: What is your main backend stack?
stack.desc: Pick the one the agent will be touching most. You can always add more later.

other.label: Something else
other.desc: We will keep the guidance stack-agnostic.

agents.title: Which AI agents do you use?
agents.desc: Pick all that apply. We will generate a folder for each — the content is the same, just rendered for the agent's format.

generic.label: Generic AGENTS.md
generic.desc: AGENTS.md for any agent that reads it

ci.title: Does your repo run CI on pull requests?
ci.desc: Lint, typecheck, tests — some or all of them.
ci.why: If not, we will add the CI hygiene skill so the agent learns to add checks as it changes code.

secrets.title: How do you handle secrets today?
secrets.desc: Be honest — the generator isn't judging. This just tailors the advice.

manager.label: Secret manager
manager.desc: Vault, Doppler, AWS Secrets Manager, Infisical.

env.label: .env files, git-ignored
env.desc: Common; works until someone commits by accident.

dotenv.label: A mix / not sure
dotenv.desc: We will add the secrets baseline skill to get you consistent.

none.label: Honestly? They're in the repo.
none.desc: We will make fixing this the agent's first priority.

Contribute.pageDescription: Add, update, retire, or delete a skill. The wizard turns your brief into a repo-aware prompt for your coding agent.
Contribute.actionHeading: What do you want to do?
Contribute.actionLede: Choose an authoring mode. We will tailor the prompt, the metadata form, and the governance expectations to match.
Contribute.metadataLede: Canonical fields the agent will write to skill.yaml. Required fields must be filled before moving on.
Contribute.contentLede: What should the skill body say, what should change, or what deprecation guidance should readers follow?
Contribute.governanceLede: Based on your edits, here is the version bump the verifier will demand. The prompt is pre-set to ask the agent for the correct version.
Contribute.handoffHeading: Hand the task to your coding agent
Contribute.handoffLede: Copy the prompt that matches your agent and paste it into the agent with the repo open.
Contribute.actionAddTagline: Create a brand-new skill.yaml and SKILL.md under skills/<group>/<slug>/.
Contribute.actionUpdateTagline: Edit metadata, the SKILL.md body, or support files while keeping identity stable.
Contribute.actionRetireTagline: Mark as deprecated or archived, set a replacement, and write a deprecation note.
Contribute.actionDeleteTagline: Advanced maintenance. Removes the skill package entirely.
Contribute.skillRequired: Please select which skill this applies to.
Contribute.deleteWarningBody: Prefer retire+archive. Only delete when the skill was accidentally added, was never released, or has no downstream consumers.
Contribute.deleteAcknowledge: I understand this is a major governance event and I accept the consequences.
Contribute.validationBlockedHint: Please fill the required fields before moving to the next step.
Contribute.templatePickerLede: We'll pre-fill category, region, targets, and disclaimer — you keep editing from there.
Contribute.templateSaudiComplianceTagline: Regulated behavior in Saudi Arabia — disclaimer on, region set, compliance category.
Contribute.templateComplianceGenericTagline: Non-regional compliance guardrails with the engineering-guidance disclaimer.
Contribute.templateSecurityTagline: Secrets, auth, and policy surfaces the agent must treat as guardrails.
Contribute.templateArchitectureTagline: Code-level discipline: testing, CI, boundaries, migrations.
Contribute.templateCustomTagline: No preset — fill every field yourself.
Contribute.hintGroup: Top-level folder under skills/. Usually matches category.
Contribute.hintSlug: Auto-derived from the English name. Edit only if you need a custom directory name.
Contribute.hintId: Auto-derived as <group>-<slug>. Edit if your catalog uses a different convention.
Contribute.hintPreviousId: For identity migrations: the id this skill used to ship under.
Contribute.hintNameEn: Short, specific, capitalized. Avoid abbreviations unreviewers know.
Contribute.hintSummaryEn: One sentence: what behavior does this skill enforce?
Contribute.hintSummaryAr: Arabic translation of the summary above.
Contribute.hintCategory: Picks the governance lane. Compliance gets the disclaimer notice.
Contribute.hintRegion: Optional. Use 'saudi-arabia' for KSA skills, leave blank for global.
Contribute.hintTargets: Every native target that will install this skill.
Contribute.hintStatus: Editorial maturity. New skills start as Draft.
Contribute.hintMaintainers: GitHub handles responsible for reviews and compliance freshness.
Contribute.hintSources: At least one authoritative source with an ISO access date.
Contribute.hintIntent: What the skill teaches. Use the outline button for a proven structure.
Contribute.hintEditSummary: Describe the intended edits in plain English. The agent reads this like a PR description.
Contribute.validationSlug: Use kebab-case: lowercase letters, digits, single hyphens.
Contribute.essentialsLede: Title, summary, category. The catalog reads these directly.
Contribute.identityLede: The folder path and skill id. We derive these automatically — override only if you must.
Contribute.advancedLede: Region, targets, status, disclaimer. Defaults work for most skills.
Contribute.attestationLede: Governance tracks who owns this skill and what it cites.
Contribute.livePreviewLede: What the AI handoff prompt will ask the agent to write.
Contribute.readinessIncomplete: Fill the required fields to continue.

ContributeViaAi.heading: Hand the authoring task to your coding agent
ContributeViaAi.lede: Copy a ready-to-run prompt for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or any repo-aware agent. The agent edits skills/** and runs the verify pipeline.
ContributeViaAi.agentClaudeTagline: Autonomously edits skills/** and runs pnpm verify:skills.
ContributeViaAi.agentCursorTagline: Paste in Cursor composer; it will apply the edits and run verify in the terminal.
ContributeViaAi.agentCodexTagline: Pass to Codex/GPT-5.4 with repo access.
ContributeViaAi.agentGenericTagline: Any agent that reads the repo and can run pnpm workspaces.
ContributeViaAi.fallbackNote: Never hand-edit apps/web/lib/skills/generated.ts — the agent regenerates it from source.
